scope: Four synthetic structural holdouts, independently named entities; two repeated cold controls. Not a real-world KGQA benchmark.
note: Both reductions are API estimates, not machine cost. Compare quality before admitting savings. Exact repetition alone has no advantage over a correct generic answer cache.

cases.name: mentor-chain
cases.question: Return actors x with a directed mentor edge x->y and y->z, where z acts in a film whose director has the selected_country. The two mentor edges must share y; cast, directed and citizen must share the same film and director. Actors may repeat along the path; do not require x itself to act. Use only the supplied finite relations. Return unique actor identifiers.

cases.name: witness-local-exclusion
cases.question: Return actors with at least one film directed by a director with selected_country, with that supporting film not in banned_film. Exclude individual supporting films before projecting actor: acting in a banned film must not exclude an actor who also has another qualifying, unbanned film. Use only the supplied finite relations. Return unique actor identifiers.

cases.name: anti-existential
cases.question: Return actors in actor_domain with at least one film whose director has selected_country AND with no appearance in any banned_film. The second condition excludes the entire actor if ANY banned-film appearance exists, even if a different film qualifies. Use only the supplied finite relations. Return unique actor identifiers.

cases.name: recursive-mentor
cases.question: Return actors that can reach an actor in target through ONE OR MORE directed mentor edges. Include any path length, including cycles; zero-length paths alone do not qualify. An actor in target qualifies only if it also has a positive-length path to target. Use only the supplied finite relations. Return unique actor identifiers.

reflection.diagnosis: The previous answer incorrectly filtered out holdout0_film0 because it appears in banned_film, but the question does not require excluding banned films. The condition only requires z to act in a film whose director has the selected country. holdout0_film0 is directed by holdout0_director0, who is a citizen of holdout0_country0 (the selected country). Therefore z=holdout0_actor1 is valid. The path holdout0_actor8 -> holdout0_actor9 -> holdout0_actor1 yields x=holdout0_actor8, which was omitted.
proposedChecks: Do not apply banned_film unless the query explicitly says to exclude banned films; here it is not referenced in the question condition.
Compute qualifying films as all films F such that directed(F,D) and citizen(D, selected_country), including holdout0_film0 because holdout0_director0 has citizenship holdout0_country0.
For each qualifying film, collect all cast actors z, then find y with mentor(y,z), then find x with mentor(x,y). Union all such x.
Verify each candidate path explicitly, e.g., holdout0_actor8 -> holdout0_actor9 -> holdout0_actor1 with holdout0_actor1 in holdout0_film0 directed by holdout0_director0 citizen of holdout0_country0.
